items.e: **MISHNA: All slaughtered offerings that were slaughtered not for their own sake,** i.e., during the slaughtering the slaughterer’s intent was to sacrifice a different offering, **are fit,** and one may continue their sacrificial rites and partake of their meat where that applies. **But** these offerings **did not satisfy the obligation of the owner,** who is therefore required to bring another offering. This is the halakha with regard to all offerings **except for the Paschal offering and the sin offering.** In those cases, if the owner sacrificed them not for their own sake, they are unfit. But there is a difference between the two exceptions. **The Paschal offering** is unfit only when sacrificed not for its sake **at its** appointed **time,** on the fourteenth day of Nisan after noon, while **the sin offering** is unfit **any time** that it is sacrificed not for its sake.
items.o: מַתְנִי׳ ** כׇּל הַזְּבָחִים ** שֶׁנִּזְבְּחוּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן – כְּשֵׁרִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ לַבְּעָלִים לְשֵׁם חוֹבָה; חוּץ מִן הַפֶּסַח וְהַחַטָּאת – הַפֶּסַח בִּזְמַנּוֹ, וְהַחַטָּאת בְּכׇל זְמַן.

items.e: **Rabbi Eliezer says: The guilt offering too** is unfit when sacrificed not for its sake. According to his opinion, the correct reading of the mishna is: **The Paschal offering** is unfit only **at its** appointed **time,** while **the sin offering and the guilt offering** are unfit **at all times. Rabbi Eliezer said** in explanation: **The sin offering is brought for** performance of **a transgression and the guilt offering is brought for** performance of **a transgression. Just as a sin offering is unfit** when sacrificed **not for its sake, so too, the guilt offering is unfit** when sacrificed **not for its sake.**
items.o: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַף הָאָשָׁם – הַפֶּסַח בִּזְמַנּוֹ, וְהַחַטָּאת וְהָאָשָׁם בְּכׇל זְמַן. אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: הַחַטָּאת בָּאָה עַל חֵטְא, וְהָאָשָׁם בָּא עַל חֵטְא; מָה חַטָּאת – פְּסוּלָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, אַף הָאָשָׁם – פָּסוּל שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ.

items.e: **Yosei ben Ḥoni says:** Not only are the Paschal offering and the sin offering unfit when slaughtered not for their sake, but also other offerings **that are slaughtered for the sake of a Paschal offering and for the sake of a sin offering are unfit.**
items.o: יוֹסֵי בֶּן חוֹנִי אוֹמֵר: הַנִּשְׁחָטִין לְשֵׁם פֶּסַח וּלְשֵׁם חַטָּאת – פְּסוּלִין.

items.e: **Shimon, brother of Azarya, says** that this is the distinction: With regard to all offerings, if **one slaughtered them for the sake of** an offering whose level of sanctity is **greater than theirs, they are fit;** if one slaughtered them **for the sake of** an offering whose level of sanctity is **less than theirs, they are unfit.**
items.o: שִׁמְעוֹן אֲחִי עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: שְׁחָטָן לְשֵׁם גָּבוֹהַּ מֵהֶן – כְּשֵׁרִין, לְשֵׁם נָמוּךְ מֵהֶן – פְּסוּלִין.

items.e: **How so? Offerings of the most sacred order,** e.g., sin offerings and burnt offerings, **that one slaughtered for the sake of offerings of lesser sanctity,** e.g., peace offerings, **are unfit. Offerings of lesser sanctity that one slaughtered for the sake of offerings of the most sacred order are fit.** Likewise, there is a distinction between different offerings of lesser sanctity. **The firstborn** animal **and the** animal **tithe that one slaughtered for the sake of a peace offering are fit,** as the sanctity of peace offerings is greater. **Peace offerings that one slaughtered for the sake of a firstborn** animal **or for the sake of** an animal **tithe are unfit.**
items.o: כֵּיצַד? קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשֵׁם קֳדָשִׁים קַלִּים – פְּסוּלִין, קֳדָשִׁים קַלִּים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשֵׁם קׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים – כְּשֵׁרִין. הַבְּכוֹר וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשֵׁם שְׁלָמִים – כְּשֵׁרִין, שְׁלָמִים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשֵׁם בְּכוֹר וּלְשֵׁם מַעֲשֵׂר – פְּסוּלִין.

items.e: **GEMARA:** The mishna teaches: All slaughtered offerings that were slaughtered not for their sake are fit, but they did not satisfy the obligation of the owner. The Gemara asks: **Why do I** need the mishna **to teach** this halakha using the language: **But they did not [ ella shelo ] satisfy** the obligation of the owner? **Let it teach** simply: **And they did not [ velo ] satisfy the obligation of the owner.** What does the word: But [ ella ], add?
items.o: ** גְּמָ׳ ** לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנָא ״אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ״? לִיתְנֵי ״וְלֹא עָלוּ לַבְּעָלִים לְשֵׁם חוֹבָה״!

items.e: The Gemara responds: By adding **this** word, the mishna **teaches us** that the only deficiency with regard to these offerings **is that they did not satisfy the obligation of the owner, but they retain their sanctity, and it is** still **prohibited to deviate** from the protocol **of their** sacrificial process, i.e., the remaining rites must be performed with proper intent.
items.o: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: לַבְּעָלִים הוּא דְּלָא עָלוּ לְשֵׁם חוֹבָה – אֲבָל בִּקְדוּשְׁתַּיְיהוּ קָיְימִי, וְאָסוּר לְשַׁנּוֹיֵי בְּהוּ.

items.e: **And** this halakha is **in accordance with** the statement **of Rava, as Rava says:** With regard to **a burnt offering that one slaughtered not for its sake,** it is still **prohibited to sprinkle its blood** on the altar **not for its sake.**
items.o: וְכִדְרָבָא, דְּאָמַר רָבָא: עוֹלָה שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ – אָסוּר לִזְרוֹק דָּמָהּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ.

items.e: The Gemara adds: **If you wish, propose a logical argument** to support this statement, and **if you wish, cite a verse** as proof. The Gemara elaborates: **If you wish, propose a logical argument:** Just **because** one **deviated** from protocol **in its** sacrifice once, i.e., in its slaughter, could it be that **he should continue to deviate** from protocol **in all** the rest of the sacrificial rites? One deviation does not justify additional deviations.
items.o: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא, אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא. אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא: מִשּׁוּם דְּשַׁנִּי בַּהּ – כָּל הָנֵי לִישַׁנֵּי בַּהּ וְלֵיזִיל?!

items.e: And **if you wish, cite a verse: “That which has gone out of your lips you shall observe and do; according to what you have vowed [ nadarta ] freely [ nedava ] to the Lord your God,** even that which you have promised with your mouth” (Deuteronomy 23:24). The Gemara interprets the words nadarta and nedava exegetically: Can **this** verse be referring to **a gift** offering [** nedava **]?
items.o: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא: ״מוֹצָא שְׂפָתֶיךָ תִּשְׁמֹר וְעָשִׂיתָ, כַּאֲשֶׁר נָדַרְתָּ לַה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ נְדָבָה וְגוֹ׳״ – הַאי נְדָבָה?!
